label: Simple Complexes of Groups
notes: This chapter, printed pages 367 to 396, opens the bridge into Part III. We learn to record a group acting on a simply connected complex by remembering only the quotient together with the cell stabilizers and the maps between them. The central question is reversing that compression: when does such bookkeeping come from a genuine action?

label: A Group Acting on a Complex
notes: Start from the concrete picture. A group acts by cellular isometries on a simply connected complex, and we slice it into a fundamental domain. Each cell of the quotient remembers the subgroup that fixed it upstairs. The unfolded complex is rich; the quotient with labels is small. Our whole subject is the dictionary between these two.

label: Stratified Spaces and Strata
notes: Before encoding groups we organise the space. A stratified space is partitioned into strata indexed by a poset, with each stratum's closure a union of lower strata. The action permutes strata, so stabilizers are constant along a stratum. This poset of strata is exactly the scaffold onto which we will hang the local group data.

label: Strict Fundamental Domain
notes: The simple case rests on a strict fundamental domain: a subcomplex meeting each orbit so that the quotient map restricted to it is a homeomorphism onto the quotient. No cell is identified with another by the group. This strictness is what lets stabilizers attach cleanly to quotient cells without choosing extra gluing data.

label: Simple Complex of Groups
notes: Here is the definition. Over the poset of cells we place a local group at each cell and an injective homomorphism whenever one cell is a face of another, all compatible under composition. That functorial assignment, born from a strict domain, is a simple complex of groups. It is the static fingerprint of a dynamic action.

label: From Action to Data
notes: Walk the forward map carefully. Given the action with strict domain, the local group is the stabilizer of a cell and each face inclusion is the literal containment of stabilizers, since fixing a larger cell forces fixing its faces. Everything commutes because these are honest subgroups of one ambient group. The data is determined, not invented.

label: The Basic Construction
notes: To reverse the arrow we need a candidate group. From a complex of groups over a domain Y we form the basic construction: glue copies of Y indexed by group elements, factoring out the local group relations. When the data came from an action this rebuilds the original complex. In general it produces our best guess at a development.

label: Fundamental Group of a Complex of Groups
notes: The reversing group is the fundamental group of the complex of groups, a colimit assembled from the local groups along the face inclusions, like a graph of groups generalised to higher dimension. Each local group maps into it. Whether those maps stay injective is precisely the subtle question of developability that we confront next.

label: Developability
notes: A complex of groups is developable when it actually arises from an action on a simply connected complex, equivalently when every local group injects into the fundamental group. Simple complexes are always developable by construction. Abstract ones need not be: the local data can be globally inconsistent, the higher-dimensional echo of an amalgam that collapses.

label: The Local Development
notes: Developability is tested locally. Around each vertex the data prescribes a link, and the candidate development unfolds that vertex into a local development whose link is built from cosets of the local groups. If every local development is a genuine complex with the right link, the global development exists. Local consistency is the lever.

label: Non-Positive Curvature Implies Developable
notes: Now the geometry pays off. Give the quotient a metric making each local development non-positively curved, so links satisfy the large-link condition. Then the basic construction is locally CAT(0), hence by the Cartan-Hadamard theorem simply connected and CAT(0). A CAT(0) space is contractible, so the action it supports proves developability. Curvature certifies consistency.

label: Synthesis and the Road to Part III
notes: Pulling the threads together: actions compress to simple complexes of groups, abstract complexes try to decompress via the basic construction and fundamental group, and a non-positive curvature condition guarantees the decompression succeeds. This local-to-global mechanism, powered by CAT(0) geometry, is the engine driving the general theory of complexes of groups in Part III.
